name: Rosa Delgado, Total Knee Replacement POD 1

caseMeta.title: Total Knee Arthroplasty (Elective) - Hospital Day 2
learningObjectives: Prepare a patient for elective total knee arthroplasty: pre-operative checklist, medication holds, NPO, antibiotic timing, consent and site verification.
Implement post-operative TKA care: neurovascular checks, incision and dressing assessment, ice/elevation, positioning, nerve block fall precautions and pain management with multimodal analgesia.
Prevent and recognize post-operative complications: DVT/PE, urinary retention, constipation, surgical-site infection, anemia and compartment syndrome.
Coordinate early mobilization with PT/OT, enoxaparin teaching and discharge planning (home health vs SNF, rolling walker).
Connect assessment findings, labs and orders to prioritize nursing care.
Safely administer medications using the MAR and linked monitoring data.

orders.name: NPO
orders.instructions: NPO after midnight for surgery; clear liquids until 2 hours before arrival were allowed per the pre-admission instructions. Sips of water with approved morning medications.

orders.name: Renal, consistent carbohydrate diet
orders.instructions: Advance as tolerated once awake and not nauseated. Heart-healthy; encourage protein and fluids. Sit upright to eat. Modified for renal, consistent carbohydrate.

orders.name: Up with assistance and fall precautions
orders.instructions: Ambulatory before surgery; fall precautions after sedation or premedication.

orders.name: Bed rest until spinal anesthesia wears off, then up with assistance
orders.instructions: Keep head of bed up 30 degrees; check sensation and movement of both legs every hour until the spinal resolves. Do NOT place a pillow under the right knee (keep the knee straight); a pillow under the heel is allowed.

orders.name: Weight bearing as tolerated right leg with rolling walker, up with assistance
orders.instructions: Out of bed to chair for meals with 1 staff and gait belt; progress with PT. Call light within reach. Nerve block can cause numbness and weakness: stand with assistance only.

orders.name: Pre-operative medication reconciliation and hold instructions
orders.instructions: Verify last dose and time of anticoagulants (apixaban, warfarin, rivaroxaban), antiplatelets, NSAIDs, GLP-1 agonists, SGLT2 inhibitors, diabetic medications, and herbal supplements. Confirm morning-of-surgery medications taken with a sip of water. Report any held-medication discrepancy to the surgeon and anesthesia.

orders.name: Pre-operative skin preparation (chlorhexidine)
orders.instructions: Chlorhexidine cloths to the right leg and body per protocol; do not shave the surgical site (clip only if needed). Confirm no open skin lesions or rash near the knee.

orders.name: Pre-operative checklist, consent and site verification
orders.instructions: Verify consent, ID and allergy bands, right knee marked by the surgeon, NPO status, last void, dentures/jewelry removed, cefazolin ready for infusion within 60 minutes before incision.

orders.name: Type and screen
orders.instructions: Blood bank specimen; armband required.

orders.name: Neurovascular checks right leg
orders.frequency: Every hour x4, then every 4 hours
orders.instructions: Check color, warmth, capillary refill, dorsalis pedis/posterior tibial pulses, sensation and ability to move toes and ankle (dorsiflexion for peroneal nerve). Compare with the other leg. Notify the surgeon for pallor, coolness, loss of pulse, new numbness, foot drop, or severe pain unrelieved by medication.
nursingConsiderations: Expect numbness over the medial knee and shin from the adductor canal block for 8-14 hours.
Tense swelling, severe pain with passive toe movement, or a cool pale foot may be compartment syndrome or arterial injury: call immediately.

orders.name: Surgical dressing and incision assessment
orders.instructions: Assess the compression dressing for strikethrough (mark and time any drainage), warmth, swelling and tightness; keep intact unless saturated or per surgeon. Expect bruising and swelling of the knee, calf and ankle.
nursingConsiderations: Report drainage that soaks through the dressing, fever above 101 F, spreading redness, or foul odor.
Do not remove skin staples; surgeon removes them at the 2-week visit.

orders.name: Cryotherapy (ice / cold therapy) and elevation
orders.frequency: 20 minutes on, 40 minutes off while awake
orders.instructions: Apply cold therapy over the dressing; place a cloth barrier between ice and skin. Elevate the leg on pillows under the calf/heel with the knee straight and heel off the bed.
nursingConsiderations: Check skin under the ice pack; the nerve block reduces cold sensation, so frostbite risk is higher.

orders.name: Continuous passive motion (CPM) machine
orders.frequency: 2 hours, three times daily from POD 0-1
orders.instructions: CPM machine on the right leg: begin at 0-40 degrees and increase about 10 degrees per day to 90 degrees as tolerated per surgeon; heel positioned in the heel cup, patient's call light and pain medication given before use.
nursingConsiderations: Stop and notify the surgeon for severe pain, numbness, or dressing saturation.
Document degrees of motion achieved; target 90 degrees flexion and full extension (0 degrees) by discharge.

orders.name: Sequential compression devices
orders.instructions: Apply to both legs (or non-operative leg only if the operative leg dressing/swelling does not allow) until fully ambulatory. Remove for walking and skin checks every shift.

orders.name: VTE prevention: early mobilization and chemoprophylaxis
orders.instructions: Ambulate at least 3 times a day starting POD 0; ankle pumps hourly while awake. First enoxaparin dose 12 hours after surgery (timed after the spinal). Assess calves for pain, warmth, swelling or tenderness.
nursingConsiderations: Chemoprophylaxis usually continues for 10-14 days (35 days for some regimens) after surgery.
Report unilateral calf swelling/pain, sudden shortness of breath, chest pain or tachycardia immediately (DVT/PE).

orders.name: Incentive spirometry
orders.instructions: Teach and encourage deep breaths with sustained inspiration; record achieved volume.
nursingConsiderations: Goal volume documented by RT/nursing; report below 50% of goal.

orders.name: Urinary retention monitoring after spinal anesthesia
orders.instructions: Patient should void within 6-8 hours after surgery. Bladder scan if no void in 6 hours, suprapubic fullness or discomfort. Straight catheter per protocol for volume above 400 mL. No indwelling catheter is placed routinely.
nursingConsiderations: Opioids and spinal anesthesia increase retention risk, especially in men with an enlarged prostate.

orders.name: Fall prevention after nerve block and opioids
orders.instructions: High fall risk: bed alarm, non-skid socks, gait belt, assist x1 for all transfers until block resolved and PT clears. Never leave on the commode alone. Keep call light and walker within reach.
nursingConsiderations: A numb or weak leg can buckle: do not let the patient stand alone for the first 12-24 hours.

orders.name: Transfusion threshold: Hgb below 7 g/dL or symptomatic
orders.instructions: Notify the surgeon for Hgb below 8 g/dL, symptomatic tachycardia, dizziness, or hypotension. Restrictive transfusion strategy (Hgb below 7 g/dL, or 8 g/dL with cardiac disease or symptoms).
nursingConsiderations: Expect a Hgb drop of about 2 g/dL below baseline by post-op day 1-2.

orders.name: Physical therapy evaluation and treatment
orders.instructions: Same-day mobilization: stand and walk with rolling walker, WBAT right leg; knee range of motion, quadriceps sets, straight leg raise, stair training before discharge.

orders.name: Occupational therapy evaluation and treatment
orders.instructions: ADL retraining, bathing and toileting with adaptive equipment (raised toilet seat, reacher, sock aid); home safety review.

orders.name: Case management consult: discharge planning
orders.instructions: Confirm home setup (stairs, support person for first 48 hours), home health PT vs short-term skilled nursing facility, durable medical equipment (rolling walker, raised toilet seat) and outpatient PT.

orders.name: Renal dosing review / avoid nephrotoxins
orders.instructions: Pharmacy to renally dose medications. Avoid NSAIDs, IV contrast when possible, and other nephrotoxic agents.
nursingConsiderations: Question any NSAID or contrast order and notify the provider.

orders.name: Skin assessment with attention to skin folds
orders.instructions: Inspect skin folds, sacrum, and heels for moisture and pressure injury.

orders.name: Bariatric / appropriate-size equipment and lift assist
orders.instructions: Use appropriately rated bed, chair and lift equipment; at least 2 staff for mobilization.

orders.name: Point-of-care blood glucose
orders.instructions: Check before meals and at bedtime; every 6 hours while NPO. Treat per hypoglycemia protocol.

orders.name: Hypoglycemia protocol
orders.instructions: Follow facility hypoglycemia protocol: 15 g fast carbohydrate if awake, recheck in 15 minutes; dextrose 50% IV if NPO or unable to swallow.

orders.name: Vital signs
orders.instructions: Notify provider for SBP below 90 or above 180, HR above 120 or below 50, RR above 28, SpO2 below 90%, or temperature above 101.5 F.

orders.name: Strict intake and output
orders.instructions: Record all oral and IV intake and all output (urine, drains, emesis).

orders.name: Fall precautions
orders.instructions: Call light in reach, bed low, non-skid footwear, assist with ambulation.

orders.name: Continuous pulse oximetry while on opioids
orders.instructions: Notify provider for SpO2 below 90% or RR below 10.

orders.name: Consult: Anesthesiology (pre-anesthesia evaluation)
orders.instructions: Anesthesia plan for right total knee arthroplasty

orders.name: Right total knee arthroplasty (cemented)
orders.instructions: Right total knee arthroplasty (cemented). Consent, NPO status and pre-op checklist before transport.
nursingConsiderations: Confirm consent is signed and in chart.
Confirm NPO status and last intake time.
Complete pre-op checklist; verify allergy band and site marking.

orders.name: X-ray right knee, AP and lateral, post-operative
orders.instructions: Perform X-ray right knee, AP and lateral, post-operative.

orders.name: 12-lead ECG
orders.instructions: Perform 12-lead ECG.

orders.name: CBC and comprehensive metabolic panel (CMP)
orders.instructions: Draw at 0500 daily. CBC plus CMP (sodium, potassium, chloride, CO2, BUN, creatinine, glucose, calcium, AST, ALT, alkaline phosphatase, bilirubin, albumin, total protein). Admission labs were drawn in the ED; the first routine AM draw is 2026-10-20 at 0500.

orders.name: Magnesium and phosphorus
orders.instructions: Draw with the 0500 labs. Replace per protocol (magnesium goal 2.0 or higher with arrhythmia risk).

orders.name: Platelet and kidney monitoring for heparin / low-molecular-weight heparin
orders.instructions: Platelets are checked every 2-3 days for heparin-induced thrombocytopenia (a fall of 50% or to below 100); creatinine is checked because enoxaparin is cleared by the kidneys. Hold and call for active bleeding or platelets below 50.

orders.name: Potassium and creatinine monitoring for diuretic / ACE inhibitor / ARB
orders.instructions: Report potassium below 3.5 or above 5.0, or a creatinine rise of 0.3 or more. Hold ACE inhibitor/ARB and call for SBP below 100 or rising creatinine/potassium.

orders.name: insulin lispro (HUMALOG) correction scale
orders.instructions: Administer Low-dose correction scale Subcutaneous ACHS (before meals and at bedtime).

medication.importantInfo: Give per correction scale only with a meal (or q6h if NPO). Check glucose first and document it. Watch for hypoglycemia.

orders.name: lisinopril (PRINIVIL,ZESTRIL) tablet
orders.instructions: Administer 20 mg Oral Daily. Hold and notify provider if SBP is below 100.
nursingConsiderations: Hold and notify provider if SBP is below 100.

medication.importantInfo: Check BP before giving. Monitor potassium and creatinine. Watch for cough and angioedema.
medication.hold: Hold and notify provider if SBP is below 100.

orders.name: pantoprazole (PROTONIX) tablet
orders.instructions: Administer 40 mg Oral Daily.

orders.name: senna-docusate (SENOKOT-S) tablet
orders.instructions: Administer 2 tablets Oral BID.

medication.importantInfo: Hold for loose stools. Goal: a bowel movement at least every other day.

orders.name: acetaminophen (TYLENOL) tablet
orders.instructions: Administer 1,000 mg Oral Every 8 hours.

medication.importantInfo: Scheduled (not PRN) base of multimodal analgesia; first dose before surgery with a sip of water. Maximum 3 g per 24 hours from all sources.

orders.name: insulin glargine (LANTUS) injection
orders.instructions: Administer 20 units Subcutaneous Nightly at bedtime. Notify provider before giving if glucose is below 100 mg/dL.
orders.rationale: Type 2 diabetes (home basal insulin, reduced 20% while NPO)
nursingConsiderations: Notify provider before giving if glucose is below 100 mg/dL.

medication.importantInfo: Basal insulin. Give even when NPO (dose reduced). Check glucose first; hold and call provider if glucose is below 100 mg/dL.
medication.hold: Notify provider before giving if glucose is below 100 mg/dL.

orders.name: atorvastatin (LIPITOR) tablet
orders.instructions: Administer 40 mg Oral Nightly at bedtime.

medication.importantInfo: Report unexplained muscle pain or weakness.

orders.name: levothyroxine (SYNTHROID) tablet
orders.instructions: Administer 75 mcg Oral Daily.

medication.importantInfo: Give on an empty stomach, 30-60 minutes before breakfast, separate from calcium/iron.

orders.name: enoxaparin (LOVENOX) injection
orders.instructions: Administer 40 mg Subcutaneous Daily. Hold and notify provider for active bleeding or platelets below 50.
nursingConsiderations: Hold and notify provider for active bleeding or platelets below 50.

medication.importantInfo: Monitor for bleeding, bruising, platelets and renal function. Never give if platelets below 50 or active bleeding.
medication.hold: Hold and notify provider for active bleeding or platelets below 50.

orders.name: hydromorphone (DILAUDID) injection
orders.instructions: Administer 0.5 mg IV Every 3 hours PRN severe pain (7-10). Hold for RR below 10, SpO2 below 90%, or sedation.
nursingConsiderations: Hold for RR below 10, SpO2 below 90%, or sedation.

medication.importantInfo: HIGH-ALERT. Assess pain, sedation (RASS), RR and SpO2 before and 15-30 minutes after. Hold for RR below 10 or oversedation.
medication.hold: Hold for RR below 10, SpO2 below 90%, or sedation.

orders.name: oxycodone (ROXICODONE) tablet
orders.instructions: Administer 5 mg Oral Every 4 hours PRN moderate pain (4-6). Hold for RR below 10 or sedation.
nursingConsiderations: Hold for RR below 10 or sedation.

medication.importantInfo: HIGH-ALERT. Give before PT when pain is 4 or higher. Assess pain and sedation before and 30-60 minutes after. Hold for RR below 10 or oversedation. Part of multimodal analgesia: use the lowest effective dose and wean to acetaminophen and celecoxib.
medication.hold: Hold for RR below 10 or sedation.

orders.name: ondansetron (ZOFRAN) injection
orders.frequency: Every 8 hours PRN nausea or vomiting
orders.instructions: Administer 4 mg IV Every 8 hours PRN nausea or vomiting.

medication.importantInfo: Post-operative nausea after spinal/sedation. Check QTc before repeated dosing in an older adult. Reassess nausea in 30 minutes.

orders.name: polyethylene glycol (MIRALAX) powder
orders.frequency: Once daily PRN no bowel movement in 24 hours
orders.instructions: Administer 17 g Oral Once daily PRN no bowel movement in 24 hours.

medication.importantInfo: Mix in 4-8 oz of fluid. Hold for loose stools. Goal: bowel movement by post-op day 2-3.

orders.name: lactated Ringer's infusion
orders.instructions: Administer 100 mL/hr IV Continuous at 100 mL/hr.

medication.importantInfo: Assess lungs, edema, I&O and daily weight. Check IV site each shift.

orders.name: cefazolin (ANCEF) IVPB
orders.instructions: Administer 2 g IV Every 12 hours.
nursingConsiderations: Interval extended for reduced kidney function.

medication.importantInfo: Surgical prophylaxis: first dose within 60 minutes before incision (and before the tourniquet is inflated), then every 8 hours for no more than 24 hours. Low cross-reactivity with penicillin; verify reaction history. Infuse over 30 minutes.

stickyNotes.title: Fall risk after block / opioids
stickyNotes.body: Spinal and adductor canal block can cause leg numbness and weakness. Assist x1 with gait belt and walker for every transfer; bed alarm on.

stickyNotes.title: Knee positioning
stickyNotes.body: No pillow under the operative knee (flexion contracture risk); pillow under the heel. Ice and elevate; neurovascular checks every 4 hours; CPM per order.

stickyNotes.title: VTE prevention
stickyNotes.body: Enoxaparin first dose 12 hours after surgery; SCDs; ankle pumps; walk 3+ times daily. Report calf pain/swelling, dyspnea or chest pain immediately.

notes.author: P. Lawson, RN, CCM
notes.summary: Anticipated discharge: Home with home health or outpatient PT, rolling walker and a family caregiver (skilled nursing facility only if needed).
notes.body:
**Social situation**
- Lives with spouse/partner. Insurance: Medicare with supplemental plan. Transportation: family/self.
- Prior function: independent with a cane for 2 years.

**Barriers**
- uses independent with a cane for 2 years at baseline

**Anticipated discharge plan**
- Home with home health or outpatient PT, rolling walker and a family caregiver (skilled nursing facility only if needed).
- Estimated discharge: post-operative day 2 (hospital day 3) once pain is controlled on oral medication, walking 100+ feet with a walker, stairs completed, voiding and Hgb stable.

**Plan**
- Follow daily for medical readiness, therapy recommendations and equipment/home health needs.

notes.title: Surgery Progress Note
notes.author: R. Alvarez, MD
notes.summary: Hospital day 2 | POD 1: Post-operative day 1: working with therapy.
notes.body:
**Hospital Day 2 | POD 1**

**Interval events / subjective**
Knee aching 4-5/10 at rest and 6/10 with therapy after the block wore off overnight. Slept poorly. Passed gas but no bowel movement. Wants to go home soon.
- X-ray right knee, AP and lateral, post-operative: Satisfactory total knee arthroplasty.

**Objective**
- Vitals (24 h): Tmax 99.5 F; HR 74-87; BP 136-150/80-85; RR 15-17; SpO2 94-96%; pain 3-6/10
- Current: T 99.5 F, HR 80, BP 142/80, RR 17, SpO2 95% on room air, pain 5/10
- I&O (24 h): in 2778 mL / out 1743 mL
- Diet: Renal, consistent carbohydrate diet; Activity: Weight bearing as tolerated right leg with rolling walker, up with assistance

**Exam**
- General: Awake and alert, in no acute distress.
- Cardiovascular: Normal sinus rhythm; S1 S2 regular, no murmur. Edema: Right knee and lower leg swollen with ecchymosis (expected); calf soft, non-tender.
- Respiratory: Clear, diminished at bases; unlabored, even.
- Abdomen: Soft, non-tender, non-distended. Bowel sounds: active in all four quadrants.
- Neurologic: Alert and oriented x4.
- Skin: Warm, dry; right knee skin intact without rash, abrasions or lesions; surgical site marked.

**Labs**
- Hemoglobin 9.9 (L) (down from 11.5); WBC 10.4 (up from 7.0); Platelets 199 (down from 240); Sodium 137 (stable from 139); Potassium 4.7 (stable from 4.7); Creatinine 1.62 (H) (up from 1.51); Glucose 193 (H) (up from 181); INR 1.0

**Medications**
- Scheduled: acetaminophen 1,000 mg Oral; insulin glargine 20 units Subcutaneous; insulin lispro correction scale Low-dose correction scale Subcutaneous; lisinopril 20 mg Oral; atorvastatin 40 mg Oral; pantoprazole 40 mg Oral; levothyroxine 75 mcg Oral; enoxaparin 40 mg Subcutaneous; senna-docusate 2 tablets Oral
- PRN: hydromorphone; oxycodone; ondansetron; polyethylene glycol powder

**Assessment and plan**
71-year-old female, hospital day 2 | POD 1.

**Primary osteoarthritis of the right knee**
- Recovering as expected. Hgb about 2 g/dL below baseline without symptoms; temperature up to 99.6 F is common after surgery; incision clean; no signs of DVT, infection, or retention.
- IV morphine stopped; oxycodone only for pain above 4 before therapy; continue acetaminophen and celecoxib.
- PT twice a day: walking, stairs practice, ROM goals 0-90 degrees; CPM per order; ice and elevation.
- Daily CBC/BMP; transfuse only for Hgb below 7-8 or symptoms.
- Continue enoxaparin and SCDs; bowel regimen (senna-docusate scheduled, Miralax PRN).
- Case management: home health vs SNF, walker and raised toilet seat ordered.

**Chronic kidney disease stage 3**
- Baseline Cr about 1.8; renally dose all medications and avoid nephrotoxins.
- Monitor BMP daily; strict I&O.

**Obesity**
- Weight-appropriate DVT prophylaxis dosing; early mobilization; skin checks every shift.

**Type 2 diabetes mellitus**
- Basal glargine with ACHS correction lispro; goal glucose 140-180 mg/dL.
- Metformin held while inpatient.
- Hypoglycemia protocol in place.

**Hypertension**
- Continue home antihypertensive; BP goal below 140/90.

**Hyperlipidemia**
- Continue statin.

**Gastroesophageal reflux disease**
- Continue pantoprazole (IV while NPO).

**Hypothyroidism**
- Continue levothyroxine when taking PO (may hold a few days if NPO); TSH on admission.

**Disposition**
- Anticipate discharge home on POD 2 if pain, mobility and stairs allow.
- Code status: Full Code.

notes.title: Nursing Progress Note
notes.author: L. Bennett, RN
notes.summary: Night shift summary: Post-operative day 1: working with therapy.
notes.body:
**Shift summary (night shift, hospital day 2 | POD 1)**
- Neuro: Alert and oriented x4. Pain: 5/10 (right knee incision, aching, 4/10 at rest; block has worn off).
- Cardiac: Normal sinus rhythm; edema: right knee and lower leg swollen with ecchymosis (expected); calf soft, non-tender. Vitals this shift: Tmax 99.5 F; HR 80-87; BP 142-150/80-85; RR 16-17; SpO2 94-96%; pain 5-6/10.
- Respiratory: Clear, diminished at bases; room air, SpO2 95%.
- GI: Soft, non-tender, non-distended; diet Renal, consistent carbohydrate diet; nausea/vomiting: none.
- GU: Voided 300 mL; no retention. I&O this shift: in 1750 mL, out 1649 mL.
- Skin / lines: Warm, dry; right knee skin intact without rash, abrasions or lesions; surgical site marked. Peripheral IV (Right forearm): infusing.
- Mobility / safety: Weight bearing as tolerated right leg with rolling walker, up with assistance; High risk: bed alarm on, call light in reach, non-skid socks, assist for all transfers.

**Events and interventions**
- Incision clean and dry; calves soft, non-tender; foot warm with brisk capillary refill.
- Voiding spontaneously; incentive spirometer 1,500 mL; lungs clear.
- Walked 60-100 feet with PT; premedicated before therapy.
- Enoxaparin injection given; abdominal wall site rotated; no bleeding.
- PRN medications this shift: 1915 hydromorphone 0.5 mg IV; 0330 hydromorphone 0.5 mg IV; 0015 oxycodone 5 mg Oral.

**Education**
- Walker use and stairs, ice and elevation, bowel regimen and fluids, enoxaparin self-injection teach-back, and signs of infection or blood clot.

**Plan / handoff**
- Activity: weight bearing as tolerated right leg with rolling walker, up with assistance. Anticipate discharge home on POD 2 if pain, mobility and stairs allow.
- Call light within reach; bed alarm per fall risk.

notes.title: Brief Operative Note
notes.author: R. Alvarez, MD
notes.summary: Right total knee arthroplasty (cemented): no complications; to PACU, then orthopedic unit.
notes.body:
**Pre-operative diagnosis**
- Severe right knee osteoarthritis

**Post-operative diagnosis**
- Severe right knee osteoarthritis

**Procedure**
- Right total knee arthroplasty (cemented)

**Surgeon / anesthesia**
- R. Alvarez, MD; Spinal anesthesia with light sedation and adductor canal block

**Findings**
- Tricompartmental osteoarthritis with eburnated bone on the medial femoral condyle and tibial plateau, osteophytes, and loss of cartilage. Good bone stock. Ligaments balanced; stable through full range of motion.

**Description**
Supine; thigh tourniquet inflated after cefazolin infusion. Medial parapatellar approach. Distal femoral, proximal tibial and patellar cuts made; trial components balanced; cemented femoral, tibial and patellar components with a polyethylene insert. Periarticular injection of local anesthetic. Wound irrigated and closed in layers over no drain. Occlusive silver-impregnated dressing with compression wrap applied; tourniquet time 70 minutes.

**EBL / fluids**
- EBL 100 mL; IV fluids 1,000 mL lactated Ringer's

**Specimens**
- None (bone fragments discarded)

**Complications**
- None

**Disposition**
- PACU, then orthopedic unit; stable.

notes.title: Adductor canal nerve block
notes.author: R. Alvarez, MD
notes.summary: Ultrasound-guided adductor canal block, right thigh
notes.body:
**Procedure**
- Adductor canal nerve block

**Indication**
- Post-operative analgesia, motor-sparing (opioid reduction)

**Findings / technique**
Ultrasound-guided adductor canal block with 20 mL of ropivacaine 0.5% (below maximum dose for weight) deposited around the saphenous nerve in the mid-thigh; good spread seen. No paresthesia or vascular puncture. Expect numbness over the medial knee and lower leg for 8-14 hours; quadriceps strength is mostly preserved but fall risk remains. Monitor for local anesthetic toxicity.

**Complications**
- None apparent. Patient tolerated the procedure; post-procedure vitals stable.

notes.title: General Surgery H&P / Consult
notes.author: R. Alvarez, MD
notes.summary: Admission H&P for primary osteoarthritis of the right knee.
notes.body:
**Chief complaint**
- Scheduled right total knee replacement for chronic knee pain

**History of present illness**
71-year-old female with years of progressive right knee pain from osteoarthritis, worse with walking, stairs and rising from a chair, now with night pain and limited to short distances. Conservative treatment has failed: weight management, activity modification, acetaminophen and topical/oral NSAIDs, physical therapy and two corticosteroid injections (last about 4 months ago). Standing radiographs show bone-on-bone tricompartmental arthritis with varus deformity. Completed pre-admission testing (labs, ECG, MRSA screen), anesthesia and primary care clearance. Arrives the morning of surgery for elective right total knee arthroplasty. NPO since midnight; took only approved morning medications with a sip of water. No fever, cough, urinary symptoms, or skin breakdown near the knee.

**Past medical history**
- Chronic kidney disease stage 3; Obesity (BMI 34.4); Type 2 diabetes mellitus (A1c 8.0%); Hypertension; Hyperlipidemia; GERD; Hypothyroidism

**Past surgical history**
- Cholecystectomy

**Home medications**
- insulin glargine (LANTUS) 20 units Subcutaneous Nightly at bedtime
- insulin lispro (HUMALOG) correction scale Low-dose correction scale Subcutaneous ACHS (before meals and at bedtime)
- lisinopril (PRINIVIL,ZESTRIL) 20 mg Oral Daily
- atorvastatin (LIPITOR) 40 mg Oral Nightly at bedtime
- pantoprazole (PROTONIX) 40 mg Oral Daily
- levothyroxine (SYNTHROID) 75 mcg Oral Daily
- (Metformin held while hospitalized (contrast, acute illness, renal risk).)

**Allergies**
- Sulfa drugs (Rash)

**Family history**
- Mother with hypertension and type 2 diabetes; father with coronary artery disease. Parent had knee replacement. No known family history of bleeding disorders, clotting disorders, or problems with anesthesia.

**Social history**
- Lives with spouse/partner; uses independent with a cane for 2 years at baseline; tobacco: never; alcohol: rare; other substances: none; Two-story home with a bedroom upstairs; daughter lives nearby.

**Review of systems**
- Positive for chronic knee pain, stiffness after rest, and difficulty with stairs. Negative for fever, chills, chest pain, dyspnea, calf pain or swelling, dysuria, new rash or skin lesions near the knee, nausea, or recent dental work or infection.

**Vitals**
- T 98.4 F, HR 74, BP 157/89, RR 15, SpO2 98% on room air, pain 5/10 | Wt 88 kg, BMI 34.4

**Physical exam**
- General: Awake and alert, in no acute distress.
- Cardiovascular: Normal sinus rhythm; S1 S2 regular, no murmur. Edema: None.
- Respiratory: Clear bilaterally; unlabored, even.
- Abdomen: Soft, non-tender, non-distended. Bowel sounds: active in all four quadrants.
- Neurologic: Alert and oriented x4.
- Skin: Warm, dry; right knee skin intact without rash, abrasions or lesions; surgical site marked.

**Data**
- Labs: Hemoglobin 11.5 (L); WBC 7.0; Platelets 240; Sodium 139; Potassium 4.7; Creatinine 1.51 (H); Glucose 181 (H)

**Assessment and plan**
71-year-old female with a history of chronic kidney disease stage 3, obesity, type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, gastroesophageal reflux disease, hypothyroidism admitted with primary osteoarthritis of the right knee.

**Primary osteoarthritis of the right knee**
- Elective total knee arthroplasty candidate, medically optimized; vital signs stable; consent and site marking in progress.
- Spinal anesthesia with adductor canal block; cefazolin within 60 minutes before incision (before the tourniquet).
- Scheduled acetaminophen and celecoxib started pre-operatively as part of multimodal analgesia.
- Type and screen, MRSA screen and pre-operative labs reviewed; hold anticoagulants, GLP-1/SGLT2 medications as directed.
- IV fluids; SCDs; post-op enoxaparin 12 hours after surgery; PT the day of surgery.

**Chronic kidney disease stage 3**
- Baseline Cr about 1.8; renally dose all medications and avoid nephrotoxins.
- Monitor BMP daily; strict I&O.

**Obesity**
- Weight-appropriate DVT prophylaxis dosing; early mobilization; skin checks every shift.

**Type 2 diabetes mellitus**
- Basal glargine (reduced 20% while NPO) with q6h correction lispro; goal glucose 140-180 mg/dL.
- Metformin held while inpatient.
- Hypoglycemia protocol in place.

**Hypertension**
- Hold lisinopril while NPO; BP parameters ordered; resume with diet.

**Hyperlipidemia**
- Continue statin.

**Gastroesophageal reflux disease**
- Continue pantoprazole (IV while NPO).

**Hypothyroidism**
- Continue levothyroxine when taking PO (may hold a few days if NPO); TSH on admission.

**Prophylaxis / code status**
- DVT prophylaxis per orders; fall precautions.
- Code status: Full Code.
